page: Amazon Web Services c7a.48xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized cloud instance built upon the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 x86_64 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance delivers 192 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing a strict one thread per core allocation for predictable processing execution. Supported hardware vector extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory totals 384 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, establishing an allocation of 2 GB per core. The instance includes no GPU acceleration and does not bundle local NVMe storage, requiring persistent data to traverse network storage. Network throughput is provisioned at a 50 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the top tier for multi-threaded compute and data manipulation metrics. Multi-core evaluation via stress-ng achieves 589,234.9 points, placing it in the top ten percent of tested systems. PassMark CPU testing scores 143,265.9, reinforced by extended vector instruction and encryption results. Memory microbenchmarks show cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 24,745.29 GB/sec, alongside large-block uncached read and write speeds of 694.5 GB/sec and 297.25 GB/sec. Application testing displays exceptional capacity in Clang software compilation, static web serving at 112.68 GB/sec, and Redis operations exceeding 326 million SET commands per second. Large language model inference yields rapid prompt processing across smaller parameter architectures, though single-core token generation remains moderate.

With a 1:2 CPU-to-RAM ratio and an absence of local disk drives, the hardware configuration channels resource allocation primarily into raw compute execution and high network capacity. This makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for pure parallel computing that does not justify the premium of high-memory tiers. However, workloads requiring ultra-low storage latency face potential architectural bottlenecks from remote network volumes. Best-fit deployments include large-scale continuous integration systems, Clang compilation farms, CPU-bound scientific simulations, batch image and video processing, and high-throughput stateless web applications.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.48xlarge is a dedicated compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture, featuring 192 physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz with x86_64 instruction support. The instance supplies 384 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 5 GHz, maintaining a compute-centric ratio of 2 GB of memory per core. Local instance storage is not included, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage. Networking performance is established at a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional top-tier throughput in multi-core stress-ng calculations, PassMark CPU benchmarks, Clang compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving, alongside strong in-memory operations like Redis SET processing. The hardware balance makes c7a.48xlarge cost-effective for highly parallelized compute jobs requiring massive core counts rather than storage or memory capacity, including continuous integration suites, scientific simulations, high-throughput web architectures, and multi-threaded data transformation.
